title: Helen Humes joins from Cincinnati
summary: Helen Humes was discovered singing in Cincinnati around the time Earle Warren joined, and gambled with the guys on the bus.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x:
BUCK CLAYTON - TAPE III
INTERVIEWED BY
MR. STANLEY DANCE
When we left off we were talking about Billie Holiday and the Famous Door.
Yes, Famous Door and Billie Holiday.
And I think you were going to say something then about Helen Humes. Where did she come in from?
Helen Humes came from Ohio. We used to play in Cincinnati and we went by a nightclub one night and heard this girl. She was originally from Kentucky.

Yes, but she was in Cincinnati in Ohio singing and she had such a beautiful voice you know, that Basie signed her. She came in about the same time as Earle Warren. He's another Ohio, another Ohio citizen. So they came in around the same time. And she stayed with us quite a long time. Much longer than Billie. But, uh-
No, but I mean with the band. I always thought she was very good. I always liked her very much.

Oh yes. She used to gamble with the guys, like we'd shoot craps on the bus for four hundred miles sometimes. And she would be right back in the back of the bus shooting craps with all the rest of us or playing poker or whatever it was. She liked to do it.
How did she and Jimmy Rushing get on?
Why did she leave ultimately, do you know?
